title: Doha Winners: ‘A Girl Unknown’ & ‘Concrete Land’ Scoop Top Prizes
summary: Doha Film Festival awards A Girl Unknown $75,000 Best Narrative; Concrete Land wins top prize.
content: Chinese director Zou Jing’s A Girl Unknown won the top $75,000 Best Narrative prize at the Doha Film Festival as the second edition of its revamped format came to a close on Friday evening. The China-set first feature follows the fate of a young girl who is found abandoned as a baby in a rubbish bin and then grows up from babyhood through to adolescence with three sets of different guardians and circumstances. The film world premiered in Cannes Critics’ Week earlier this year where it won the Fipresci Prize. The picture was acquired for the U.S. by Greenwich Entertainment which is planning an early 2027 tour and release. The film world premiered in Sundance, where it won the World Cinema Special Jury Award. The film is the Philippines’ entry for the 99th Academy Awards. Watch on Deadline Best Actress was awarded posthumously to Josette Kwanya for her performance in her son Auguste Bernard Kouemo’s House of the Wind as an elderly Cameroonian woman waiting for her children to return home after they left for Europe in search of fresh life opportunities. The film won Venice’s Lion of the Future for a Debut Film when it premiered there in its Orizzonti sidebar in September. This year’s jury was presided over by Japanese director Naomi Kawase, who was joined by by Oscar-winning documentarian Gianfranco Rosi, rising actor Adam Bessa, Tunisian producer Dora Bouchoucha and Palestinian director Kamal Aljafari. title: Anurag Kashyap, Ranjan Singh Back Haryana-Rooted Short ‘The Melody of Destiny’ as Executive Producers (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Anurag Kashyap and Ranjan Singh board The Melody of Destiny as presenters and executive producers.
content: Indian auteur Anurag Kashyap (“Gangs of Wasseypur”) and producer Ranjan Singh have boarded “ The Melody of Destiny ,” a short film rooted in the northern Indian state of Haryana, as presenters and executive producers, backing the film on the festival circuit. The short is the first film from Chaitanya Chugh, a 24-year-old self-taught director from Pehowa, Haryana. He produced it with Diya Panjwani and Aabhar S Dev. Related Stories ‘A Girl Unknown,’ ‘Crawling Into Myself,’ ‘Concrete Land’ Take Main Prizes at Doha Film Festival Trump Advisor Steven Paul Hopes U.S. Tax Credit Will Be 'Active' in January, Tariffs Are Old News: ‘Now It’s All Hands on Deck Federal Credit’ Saurabh Bansal plays Rajesh, who lives in Delhi, far from his wife and daughter in Haryana, and sings on the city’s streets in secret. He is saving for the day his daughter Priya (Miraya Sehgal), 10, gets married. She lives at home with her mother, Savitri (Nagmeet Arora). One evening, a conversation over dinner turns into a fight, and the family’s strained relationships come out into the open. Chugh shot the film guerrilla-style on Delhi’s streets. The idea came from two moments in his own life after the COVID-19 lockdown. In 2021, his mother told him she had given a saree from her wedding to a street performer who was collecting money for his daughter’s marriage. Months later, on the way to the mountains, Chugh saw a roadside banner offering 51 wedding items for INR 51,000 ($530), and the two memories came together. “Initially drawn from the stark reality of the importance of marriages in India, which is maligned by the illegal practice of dowry, it grew into an exploration of gendered roles and power, and how they shape family dynamics, especially in traditional setups. By looking into a household whose relationships are governed by abuse rooted in the problems of class and patriarchy, the film tries to present a documentation of these gruesome truths,” Chugh said. title: Denis Villeneuve “Deeply Disappointed” That ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Will Launch On Same Weekend As ‘Dune: Part Three’
summary: Denis Villeneuve laments Disney's December 18 Avengers: Doomsday opening against Warner Bros.' Dune: Part Three.
content: Denis Villeneuve says he is “deeply disappointed” that Disney chose to release box office juggernaut Avengers: Doomsday over the same December 18 weekend as the third instalment in his Dune franchise. In a new interview with Time Magazine, Villeneuve said his first two Dune films had to contend with the tail end of the pandemic and then the Hollywood strikes, respectively, something he described as “rough” and “not easy”. With the third film, he thought he and Warner Bros were out of the woods. Then came news that Disney was dropping into the same release weekend with Avengers . Related Stories News 'Avengers: Doomsday' U.S. Presales Now At $100M+ As Pic Heads For $270M+ Opening - Box Office News Chris Evans On Secret Meetings About 'Avengers' Return Despite Saying He Was "Happily Retired" From MCU He expanded: “Disney put the biggest franchise of all time against us. I’m no fool. Those movies are a mammoth. So I was deeply disappointed. But we had committed to this date, to IMAX. It was impossible to move. So I accepted my fate, praying to the gods of cinema. Dune is not a mammoth like the Avengers, but it’s a sexy little animal that has a lot of firepower, and I hope we will survive. It could be one of the biggest box-office weekends of all time because of both movies. Am I in competition with the Avengers ? Absolutely not. It’s a T. rex. But I stand proud because I think the film delivers.”” Watch on Deadline My colleague Anthony had a report earlier this week looking at both films’ domestic box office outlook. NRG tracking has Avengers gunning for a $270M+ start with a shot at $300M and Dune eyeing a $75M-80M start. The former is NRG’s biggest ever opening weekend projection. The latter would be close to Dune: Part Two ‘s first domestic weekend. The Time interview also touched on Villeneuve’s upcoming James Bond film. title: Huw Edwards Channel 4 Doc Slammed by U.K. Prime Minister: ‘We Have No Interest in Hearing What He Has to Say’
summary: UK PM Andy Burnham criticizes Huw Edwards — Guilty documentary at Channel 4, Dec. 1.
content: U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham ‘s office has spoken out against an upcoming Channel 4 documentary featuring an interview with disgraced former BBC presenter Huw Edwards . Announced on Thursday , the doc sees Edwards — who, in 2024, was convicted of three counts of making indecent images of children and given a six-month suspended sentence — speak publicly about his downfall and criminal actions for the first time. Titled “Huw Edwards — Guilty,” it’s set to air on Channel 4 Dec. 1. Related Stories Doha Film Festival Opens With Message of Resilience Amongst Geopolitical Turmoil: Filmmaking ‘Brings Humanity to the Headlines’ Muayad Alayan on His Jerusalem-Set Drama 'Conversation With the Sea':'You Cannot Avoid the Almost Two Million Palestinians Living in Israel' The doc has stirred up quite a bit of backlash in the U.K., with several members of Parliament speaking out against it, and now Burnham has added his voice to the mix. In a statement to BBC News , an official spokesperson said: “Our thoughts first and foremost will be with the victims of child sexual abuse and exploitation. We have no interest in hearing what he has to say.” The spokesperson added that these “are extremely serious crimes and anyone convicted of them must face the consequences of their actions” and said that broadcasters “are expected to act responsibly and have appropriate regards to their audiences when making decisions.” Asked if the prime minister believed Channel 4 has not acted responsibly by making the documentary, the spokesperson said: “Channel 4 is editorially independent and decisions about individual programmes and contributors are a matter for them.” A spokesperson for Channel 4 told Variety : “Channel 4 has an established reputation for producing high-quality, forensic documentaries alongside a remit to cover challenging and controversial issues of public interest.
